6 numbers that
can save your trip.
slides.kicker: Most travellers in India don't know which emergency number does what. **This carousel is the whole answer** — every number verified against official government sources.

rows.text: **No guesswork.** Each number below is cross-checked against 112.gov.in and incredibleindia.gov.in.
**Save it now.** You won't have signal to google this when you actually need it.

slides.label: Why this matters
slides.title:
Why this
matters.
slides.kicker: India has **different numbers for different emergencies** — and tourists rarely learn them before something goes wrong.

rows.text: In the mountains, help can be **hours away**. Calling the right line first matters.
Foreign SIMs and eSIMs work with these lines — **112 connects even on another carrier's network.**
The tourist helpline runs **24×7 in multiple languages**, including English and Hindi.
**Police, fire and ambulance** — one number, anywhere in India.
When in doubt, **dial 112 first.** The operator routes you.
**108 — Ambulance.** Free emergency medical response, pan-India.
**101 — Fire.** The dedicated fire brigade line.
**100 — Police.** The legacy police line still works everywhere.

note.text: free to call. no SIM credit needed.

rows.text: **1800-11-1363 — Tourist Helpline.** Ministry of Tourism, 24×7, multilingual. Scams, lost documents, guidance.
**1091 — Women's Helpline.** Dedicated support line for women in distress.
Every NakshIQ destination page carries **local hospital and rescue contacts** on top of these.
